tasks.spec:
You are a code worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. Edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit, push or touch .git. You own only: scripts/ringer/affordance/cue_eligibility_compare.py (new) and tests/test_cue_eligibility_compare.py (new). Do NOT edit storygame/ (especially not storygame/runtime/engine.py), data/, or any other file. This is a REPORT; it must not change any runtime behaviour.

BACKGROUND. A scene can show the player a cue: one scene-description sentence (`cue_text` in data/stories/continuity-initiative/handoffs.yaml, one per fact delivery) that points at an action to take. In storygame/runtime/engine.py, `RuntimeEngine._cue_reveal_available(fact_id)` decides whether a cue may be shown: it finds the scene's reveals (knowledge items) that assert the cue fact (or that fact's delivery cost facts) and returns True if there are none or if any of them has all its `requires` predicates true. It does NOT look at whether the reveal's source storylet is already spent, whether the reveal is already established, or whether its storylet is active. The shared function `explain_reveal(state, audience_id, item)` in storygame/runtime/reveal_eligibility.py returns the first reason a reveal is not eligible: already_established, not_visible, storylet_spent, prerequisite_missing, source_inactive, or eligible. We want to know where the cue check and explain_reveal disagree, BEFORE anyone changes the engine. Story design note: storylets are optional pressure, never blocking; the timer ends a scene. A cue pointing at a reveal that is already spent is the defect class (the player is invited to an action that can no longer answer).

TASK. Write scripts/ringer/affordance/cue_eligibility_compare.py (importable, with `report(package) -> str`, and a `main` that prints it; run as `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python scripts/ringer/affordance/cue_eligibility_compare.py [package_dir]`, default data/stories/continuity-initiative). Read scripts/ringer/affordance/sibling_reachability.py first: it already builds states (`_state`, `_apply_reveal`, `_activate_unfired_storylets`, seeding of prerequisites) with RuntimeState.model_construct; reuse or import its helpers. To call the REAL `_cue_reveal_available` you need a RuntimeEngine bound to that state; find how tests build one (tests/test_3c_cue_chain.py, `RuntimeEngine(...)`), or call the method unbound on a minimal object that has `.state`, but only if it runs the real method body unchanged.
For every scene and every delivery that has `cue_text`, and for each of these states: (S0) scene entry with every storylet of the scene active whose activation holds, nothing fired; (S1..Sn) each storylet of the scene fired once through each of its reveals, one at a time (apply the reveal's establishes, mark the storylet fired, seed prerequisites the way sibling_reachability does, then activate unfired storylets), print one row per (state, cue fact): scene, state label, cue fact, `_cue_reveal_available` result (True/False), and for the reveals that assert the cue fact (or its delivery cost facts, same rule the engine uses) the explain_reveal reason of each, and a classification:
  AGREE (both mean available, or both mean unavailable),
  CUE_SHOWN_BUT_SPENT (cue True while every such reveal is storylet_spent),
  CUE_SHOWN_BUT_EARNED (cue True while the reveal is already_established),
  CUE_SHOWN_BUT_INACTIVE (cue True while the only reasons are source_inactive, which may just mean the storylet has not become active yet; this one is RISKY to suppress, say so in the report heading),
  CUE_SHOWN_BUT_HIDDEN (not_visible),
  OTHER (anything else; print the reasons).
Skip reveals whose audience is world_only (player cannot earn them). End the report with counts per classification and a plain-language list of every CUE_SHOWN_BUT_SPENT row (these are the invitations that point at a spent reveal). The report states its limit: only the states listed are covered, it is not exhaustive. Exit 0 always.
Include in the report the known case: scene 1A, state 'SL-1A-B fired through k_sl_1a_b_r1', cue fact continuity_initiative_known, expected CUE_SHOWN_BUT_SPENT. If your run does not show it, say so loudly in notes.md and do not hide it.

TESTS. tests/test_cue_eligibility_compare.py: (1) a hermetic synthetic-package test (reuse the synthetic helper in tests/test_sibling_reachability.py or tests/test_reveal_eligibility.py) with a cue whose reveal is spent: classified CUE_SHOWN_BUT_SPENT; a cue whose reveal is eligible: AGREE; one whose reveal is already established: CUE_SHOWN_BUT_EARNED; one with a missing prerequisite: AGREE (both unavailable). (2) a real-package test that the 1A known case appears as CUE_SHOWN_BUT_SPENT. (3) a test that the script does not modify runtime behaviour: `_cue_reveal_available` called before and after importing the script gives the same results on the real package.

HOW TO RUN TESTS. `uv run` does not work in this sandbox. Use `PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_cue_eligibility_compare.py`, after confirming `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame;print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside your working directory. Ruff with the same interpreter: `-m ruff check --fix . && -m ruff format .` (not on YAML or markdown). Run the full suite once at the end.

OUTPUT. notes.md at the worktree root: files, test counts, the full report for the real package, the CUE_SHOWN_BUT_SPENT list, and the counts per classification. Do not claim the suite passes unless you saw it pass.
tasks.verified: report shows where the cue check and explain_reveal disagree, including the 1A spent-reveal case; no runtime change; suite and ruff pass
